extracted.intended_audience: general public (residents of the Southern District of Indiana), media, victims' advocates
extracted.subtask_description: A Department of Justice press release announcing the conviction and sentencing in a criminal child pornography case, summarizing investigation, evidence, sentence, and related programmatic context. Intended to inform the public and media about the case and enforcement efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentencing components and conditions for child pornography conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: SCOTT HATFIELD was sentenced to 84 months imprisonment and was also imposed lifetime supervised release following release from imprisonment; HATFIELD was fined $1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chief Judge Hamilton also imposed lifetime supervised release. During the period of supervised release, HATFIELD must not have any unsupervised contact with minor children without permission of the probation department and submit to search and seizure. (These are presented as the sentencing elements and conditions ordered in this case.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and investigative steps used in prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigation identified trading of images via Limewire; a search warrant at the defendant's residence uncovered numerous hard drives networked together; the defendant identified which computer contained child pornography and the search terms he used; quantities of material were documented (approximately 58 videofiles and a folder of ~2700 images).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press release highlights the types of evidence and investigative actions supporting prosecution: identification of file-sharing activity, execution of a search warrant, seizure of storage media, defendant admission/identification of specific drives and search terms, and cataloging/counting of illicit files (used to show scope).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of interagency collaboration in child exploitation investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: This case was the result of an investigation by the Indiana State Police and Department of Homeland Security, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), with prosecution by the U.S. Attorney's Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release emphasizes coordination among state and federal agencies as instrumental to investigating and prosecuting Internet child-exploitation cases; such collaboration is framed as a standard part of enforcement practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Safe Childhood objectives and approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Safe Childhood is described as a nationwide initiative that 'marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The programmatic guidance presented: led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), it coordinates resources to combat child sexual exploitation and abuse online. The release directs readers to www.projectsafechildhood.gov for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of peer-to-peer file-sharing as a mode of distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Limewire is characterized as 'a software designed to efficiently trade any type of computer files' and that 'On the internet, individuals use Limewire most often to trade software, music, and images and videofiles of adult and child pornography.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement identifies P2P file‑sharing networks as common distribution channels for illicit material and implicitly as a focus of investigative attention; it provides context about how illicit files are shared and discovered in investigations.
